claims.text: The targeted material family is face-centered-cubic high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system.
Representative compositions include equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and Co-rich fcc variants.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms a chemically disordered fcc solid solution at ambient pressure.
The target alloys possess significant lattice distortion.
In fcc CoCrNi, Cr preferentially occupies face-centered positions while Co and Ni preferentially occupy cube-corner positions.
Strong spin-orbit coupling induced by local chemical ordering and lattice distortion suppresses the orbital contribution to saturation magnetization.
Specific solutes can increase the orbital-to-spin moment ratio without compromising fcc phase stability.
Minor additions such as Zr, Al, or other transition metals can modify lattice distortion while retaining the fcc structure.
Cold rolling followed by annealing can induce targeted local chemical ordering while maintaining the fcc phase.
Fcc CoCrFeMnNi undergoes transitions from a disordered paramagnetic state to a spin glass and then to ferromagnetic order at approximately 93 K and 38 K, respectively.
Nanometer-scale local chemical ordering in CoCrNi can be observed by atom-probe tomography.
Local chemical ordering and lattice distortion alter the electronic band structure and spin-orbit coupling strength.
Orbital angular momentum is quenched by strong crystal-field splitting and spin-orbit coupling in the distorted fcc lattice.
The arrangement of Fe, Co, Ni, Cr, and Mn modulates orbital-moment quenching.
Cr moments can align antiferromagnetically relative to their first coordination shell and thereby reduce the net magnetic moment.
Tuning ordering and distortion will enhance the orbital contribution to the total magnetic moment.
The proposed intervention will increase saturation magnetization and/or the orbital-to-spin moment ratio.
The magnetic improvement can be achieved while retaining the characteristic high strength-ductility combination of fcc high-entropy alloys.
Fcc high-entropy alloys exhibit impressive strength-ductility combinations, especially under cryogenic conditions.
The current state of the art lacks quantitative understanding and control of the orbital-moment contribution in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys.
